invariants.name: accumulator-and-countdown-model-checked
invariants.description: The same claim over the same functions, encoded for bounded model checking (L0 floor + L1 Kani)

plan.objective: Prove on production that the 0.13.0 proof ladder is live in ONE Job: the same claim is carried by three machine rungs (L0 executable check, L1 bounded model checking via Kani, L2 unbounded proof via Creusot/Why3) inside one attempt, the Job is accepted, and the signed report keeps the three decisions apart and bound to the same source tree, with the bounded rung labelled bounded.
constraints: the contract must not change mid-Job (a changed contract is a new Job, not a repair)
one attempt is expected to be enough
assumptions: the job image carries Kani 0.68.0 + CBMC 6.11.0 and Creusot v0.14.0 (why3find 1.3.0+dev, Alt-Ergo 2.6.4, Z3 5.1.0) pre-baked and offline
creusot-std resolves from the image's primed registry cache, so the job needs no network

work_items.outcome: Both invariants carry a frozen executable check and both run every attempt; the report carries an L0 row per invariant.

acceptance.description: Both check argvs exit 0 and print the expected summary line; an invariant without a check is refused BAD_CONTRACT before anything is published.

evidence.description: the two frozen check argvs run in the job container every attempt

failure_conditions: an invariant without a check is accepted
a check runs but its decision never reaches the report

omission_risks: the L0 floor being reported as if it proved the sentence rather than the encoding

work_items.outcome: The Kani rung runs kani-driver on proofs/ladder_kani.rs in the job container and returns PROVEN within the harness's own unwind bound, recorded as bounded.

acceptance.description: The signed report carries an L1 row naming the kani rung with a bounded proven decision; a missing harness is UNAVAILABLE and must not yield accepted.

evidence.description: the kani rung over the published harness file

failure_conditions: the rung is UNAVAILABLE because the harness was not published
an unbounded harness runs until the wall clock kills it and the verdict is still accepted

acceptance.description: The bounded decision is labelled bounded wherever it is presented, so a reader cannot mistake it for the unbounded claim.

evidence.description: the L1 row's rung label and bounded marker in the signed JSON report

failure_conditions: L1 proven presented as proof for all inputs

omission_risks: a bounded proven being read as a proof for all inputs

work_items.outcome: The Creusot rung discharges both goals for loop_add and countdown with no trusted item, so the claim holds for ALL inputs and not merely up to a bound.

acceptance.description: The L2 row records proven with 2/2 goals and an empty trust set; an undecided or unavailable L2 must never yield accepted (DP-13.3).

evidence.description: the creusot rung over targets loop_add and countdown

failure_conditions: goals reported proven without artifacts to back them
an undecided L2 still yielding accepted

omission_risks: a model axiom or trusted item quietly standing in for the proof

overall_acceptance.description: The Job reaches accepted on attempt 1 and the signed report carries the three rungs as distinct rows (L0 twice, L1 proven-bounded, L2 proven with 2/2 goals and no model axiom), each naming its rung; exactly one entitlement is spent at the terminal verdict; the report verifies locally with its embedded Ed25519 key.

evidence.description: the signed report's rung rows and their decisions

failure_conditions: a rung is silently skipped or reported as a pass with no decision
the verdict is accepted while any rung is unavailable or undecided
more than one entitlement is spent

overall_acceptance.description: The workspace publishes and verifies with no host-side source store and no network: the shim streams the snapshot over HTTPS, the job builds --offline, and creusot-std resolves from the image's primed cache.

evidence.description: the offline build criterion passes inside the job container

failure_conditions: the publish requires a host FG_SOURCE_STORE

limitations: osv-scanner checks registry-based ecosystems (crates.io in 0.6.0); git-sourced dependencies (lean [[require]], gpr) have no advisory database — Insufficient Evidence for them, never a silent pass
license facts are the job dependency manifest's registry SPDX ids; the workspace's own code and git-sourced dependencies carry no registry license facts
